title: Beam Hall
summary: Steer proton and electron beams in a hospital beam hall: kick them into rooms, float a test rod, tune a cyclotron and focus a gun.
subject: physics
concepts: Lorentz force F = qv × B, reversed for negative charges
Force on a wire F = BIl sin θ, balancing its weight
Circular motion in a field, r = mv/qB
Lap frequency f = qB/2πm, independent of speed
Helical motion: width from v sin θ, pitch from v cos θ
The magnetic force bends a path but does no work
learningOutcome: The student can find the direction and size of the magnetic force on a charge or a wire, and use r = mv/qB, f = qB/2πm and the pitch of a helix to steer real beams.

levels.title: Kick to the room
levels.adds: Baseline: F = qv × B is at right angles to v and B, has size qvB, and reverses for an electron (Example 4.2).
hints: The push is at right angles to both the velocity and the field.
Right-hand rule for a + charge: fingers along v, bend them towards B, and the thumb gives F. Reverse it for an electron.
Size: F = qvB, so B = F/qv with q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C.

levels.title: Float the test rod
levels.adds: New idea: a wire feels F = BIl sin θ; make it equal to the weight mg and the rod floats (Ex 4.5, 4.6, Example 4.1).
hints: Only the part of the field across the rod counts: B sin θ.
To float, BIl sin θ = mg. Change grams to kilograms and centimetres to metres.
The push must point up: use the right-hand rule with the current and the field.

levels.title: Tune the cyclotron
levels.adds: New idea: the push bends a proton into a circle, r = mv/qB, and one lap takes 2πm/qB at any speed (Ex 4.11, 4.12, Example 4.3).
hints: qvB = mv²/r gives r = mv/qB, so B = mv/qr.
The RF must kick once per lap: f = qB/2πm.
Use m = 1.67 × 10⁻²⁷ kg and q = 1.6 × 10⁻¹⁹ C, and give f in MHz.

levels.title: A new speed
levels.adds: Misconception check: a faster proton circles wider but laps in the same time, so only the port moves (Ex 4.12).
hints: r = mv/qB: the radius grows in proportion to the speed.
Look at f = qB/2πm: is the speed in it?

levels.title: Focus the gun
levels.adds: More steps: split v along and across B; the width uses v sin θ and the pitch is v cos θ × 2πm/qB (Section 4.3).
hints: Across the field: the circle’s width, 2mv sin θ/qB, must fit inside the tube.
Along the field: one turn takes T = 2πm/qB, so the pitch is v cos θ × T.
Set the pitch equal to the screen distance and solve for B. 1 G = 10⁻⁴ T.

misconceptions: The magnetic force acts along the direction of the velocity
A faster charge takes less time to go round its circle
A magnetic field speeds the particle up
An electron and a proton are pushed the same way
A wire lying along the field feels the biggest force
